# Flow factual review — 2026-10-19

The author-supplied manuscript is reproduced unchanged. This working note records checks for a later editorial pass; it is not part of the reader.

| Manuscript claim | Check |
|---|---|
| Vietnam entered the World Bank's upper-middle-income group in 2026. | [World Bank country page](https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/country/vietnam) confirms the classification. |
| Vietcombank published a 5.9% 12-month deposit rate in October 2026. | [Vietcombank's rate table](https://www.vietcombank.com.vn/en/Personal/Cong-cu-Tien-ich/KHCN---Lai-suat) is the source; the chapter clearly uses it as a dated illustrative rate. |
| Nine-month CPI rose 4.52%, with rent up around 4.91%. | [Vietnam National Statistics Office, September 2026 price release](https://www.nso.gov.vn/tin-tuc-thong-ke/2026/10/thong-cao-bao-chi-ve-tinh-hinh-gia-thang-chin-quy-iii-va-9-thang-nam-2026/) reports both figures. |
| Vietnam stock-market capitalization was about VND 10,306.94 trillion at 30 September 2026. | [Vietnam National Statistics Office, Q3 2026 release](https://www.nso.gov.vn/du-lieu-va-so-lieu-thong-ke/2026/10/thong-cao-bao-chi-tinh-hinh-kinh-te-xa-hoi-quy-iii-va-9-thang-nam-2026/) reports the figure. The manuscript's roughly USD 396 billion conversion follows its stated illustrative VND 26,000/USD assumption. |
| FTSE Russell's Secondary Emerging reclassification took effect in September 2026. | [FTSE Russell's announcement](https://www.lseg.com/en/media-centre/press-releases/ftse-russell/2025/ftse-russell-country-classification-september-2025) gives 21 September 2026, and its [April 2026 interim review](https://www.lseg.com/content/dam/ftse-russell/en_us/documents/country-classification/ftse-interim-country-classification-review-2026.pdf) confirms the schedule. |

The manuscript's explicit hypothetical arithmetic also checks out: 240 million / 10 billion = 2.4% gross rent yield; VND 5 million invested monthly for 22 years at a hypothetical 10% nominal annual rate with monthly compounding is about VND 4.766 billion. The USD 1.5 trillion real-estate value is attributed in the essay to an individual expert estimate rather than official market measurement; retain that attribution and independently verify the underlying interview for print. Personal bank transactions and forward-looking returns cannot be verified from the supplied files. None of the examples should be read as a guaranteed investment outcome.
